recentItems.title: Witnesses in the formal inquest of Anele Tembe testify in the Cape Town Magistrates Court
recentItems.description:
Witnesses in the formal inquest of Anele Tembe, the fiancée of late rapper Kiernan AKA Forbes, have testified in the Cape Town Magistrates Court that they found the hotel room occupied by the couple upside down, filthy with blood stains on the bedding, towels and a bathroom wall, as well as around a champagne bottle found on a chair. A fourth witness, Robert Staffanutto, who stays close to the hotel, said he heard loud shouting between a couple, with a female voice saying Leave me alone and get away from me. Later, he heard a wailing scream of a woman followed by a loud bang and a male voice saying Oh my God, oh my God, " twice. Tembe fell from the tenth floor of a hotel in the Cape Town CBD in April 2026. Six witnesses have been called in to testify

recentItems.title: KZN authorities inspect companies over labour compliance
recentItems.description:
KwaZulu-Natal authorities are tightening the screws on businesses accused of employing undocumented foreign nationals. 

Premier Thami Ntuli says September will see intensified enforcement operations under Operation Engangeni Ngesango Iyafohla, with raids targeting companies suspected of violating immigration and labour laws in and around the Mandeni Municipality.

Speaking during a compliance operation, Ntuli voiced concern after finding that several of the businesses earmarked for inspection had shut their doors before officials arrived. 

But he insists the closures will not derail the crackdown.

recentItems.title: Kruger Recovery | SANParks rebuilds tourism infrastructure across the park
recentItems.description:
Tourism Month gets underway with the reopening of the reconstructed Letaba Rest Camp in the northern Kruger National Park.

The camp, situated along the Letaba River, was badly damaged by floods earlier this year and has now been restored as SANParks continues rebuilding other affected camps across the park.

Minister of Fisheries, Forestry and Environment David Maynier will also officially open a new bridge as part of the park's recovery efforts.

For more on the reopening we cross live to SABC News reporter Katlego Nyoni at Letaba in the Kruger National Park, Limpopo.

For more news, visit sabcnews.com and #SABCNews on all Social Media platforms.

recentItems.title: Joburg up for grabs in 2026 municipal polls
recentItems.description:
Johannesburg's highly contested mayoral race will ultimately require candidates to do more than simply promise change.

They will have to convince an increasingly frustrated electorate that they have credible and practical plans to tackle crime, unemployment, corruption, deteriorating infrastructure and other social ills.

For many residents, the election is becoming a question of who can govern — and deliver.

Crime and lawlessness remain major concerns, but voters are also grappling with failing infrastructure, water shortages, unreliable services, damaged roads and growing economic pressure.

recentItems.title: SAFA: AmaZulu Sandile Zungu challenges Danny Jordaan for the position of President of the federation
recentItems.description:
AmaZulu chairman, Sandile Zungu, is up against Danny Jordaan for president of the federation. 

With the SAFA elective conference taking place on Saturday, candidates are giving it one last push to try and persuade delegates to vote for them. 

He’ll address the media in Johannesburg this morning and will probably highlight SAFA’s failures under the current administration to garner more support. Stay tuned as we bring you the latest

recentItems.title: Court dismisses Mapisa-Nqakula’s discharge application
recentItems.description:
The Gauteng High Court in Pretoria is handing down its decision on former National Assembly Speaker Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula's request to have her corruption and money-laundering case dismissed.

Mapisa-Nqakula says the State has not provided enough evidence against her. 

The State disagrees and says it has enough evidence for the trial to continue.

Mapisa-Nqakula is accused of asking for millions of rands in bribes while she was Defence and Military Veterans Minister.

She has always denied the allegations.

recentItems.title: SAFA Presidential candidate wants Bafana and Banyana become winners in FIFA World Cup tournaments
recentItems.description:
SAFA Presidential candidate Sandile Zungu says that his mission is to see Bafana Bafana and Banyana become the first African teams to win their respective FIFA World Cup tournaments. 

Zungu is addressing the media at the Maslow Hotel in Sandton. The SAFA elections will take place on Saturday. Zungu and the incumbent President Danny Jordaan will be the two contestants.
